knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built by dividing running costs and income by billable hours, so the work that can be billed covers them. Using all paid hours, a vendor's per-square-metre range or a wished-for rate does not do this.
The lesson says travel and set-up time do not shrink with a small job, so a minimum charge covers the visit. It does not replace a written quote, and clients do not all pay the same.

The lesson says to compare a vendor range with your own hours and rate, and notes that the hours behind the range are not stated. Copying it as your rate or ignoring it altogether is not the lesson's advice.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, visits, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
